newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, LME stock hike awaited.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, LME stock hike awaited.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer, making healthy gains on good volume with spot metal ending at its highest since just before the Sumitomo crash last June, despite expectations of a hike in LME stocks, traders said.
William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said LME copper stocks were expected to rise 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes Tuesday.
"The market has been expecting a little bit of a stock increase for a while, and then as we move into February, we will start to see a decline," O'Neill said.
Traders expected U.S. based LME stocks to rise because of metal coming from COMEX depots as a result of arbitrage.
Most active March settled 1.70 cents higher at 107.55 cents per pound, traded 108.00 to 104.50 cents. Spot January went out 2.05 cents higher at 110.35 cents.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots compared to Friday's official 6,596 lots.

The market was being driven higher by a widening backwardation on LME which rose some $20 to $234/$238 Monday, causing prompting nervousness and shortcovering among some players while stocks remain relatively low, traders said.
Much of backwardation is due to tightness on LME between the end of January and mid-February.
Good performances in other base metals, particularly zinc, nickel and even lead and aluminum were also helping copper consolidate and make gains, O'Neill said.
